lines.text: A small country of Alps, lakes and caves, ruled by others for a thousand years before it went its own way. This is the story of Slovenia.
Some five thousand years ago, in the marshes near Ljubljana, someone made a wooden wheel. It is the oldest ever found.
In the seventh century, Slavic settlers founded Carantania, one of the first Slavic states.
For centuries the land was ruled by the Habsburgs. In 1508 Primoz Trubar was born, who printed the first books in Slovene.
In 1800 came France Preseren, the national poet, whose verses are now the anthem.
After the First World War Slovenia joined Yugoslavia. In 1949 Slavoj Zizek was born in Ljubljana, the philosopher known the world over.
In 1968 Natasa Pirc Musar was born, who in 2022 would become Slovenia's first woman president.
In 1991 Yugoslavia began to break apart, in the deadliest wars Europe had seen since 1945.
Slovenia was the first to leave, declaring independence in June 1991.
The Yugoslav army struck back, but after just ten days of fighting it withdrew, and Slovenia was free.
In 1998 Tadej Pogacar was born, the cyclist who would win the Tour de France again and again.
A year later came Luka Doncic, who grew into one of the brightest stars in basketball.
And in 2004 Slovenia joined the European Union, one of ten countries to join together.
From the oldest wheel to the yellow jersey, Slovenia has found its own road.
